chunks: As for what Ali ibn Ibrahim narrated from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Jamil, from Zurara, from Abu Ja'far (AS):
he said: The shortening [of prayer] is at [the distance of] a barid, and a barid is four farsakhs.

key_terms.التَّقْصِيرُ: shortening (qasr) of prayer — the Shia jurisprudential ruling to reduce four-unit (rak'ah) prayers to two units while travelling the requisite distance
key_terms.بَرِيدٍ: barid — a postal/road distance unit; here defined as four farsakhs (approx. 22–23 km)
key_terms.فَرَاسِخَ: farsakhs (sing. farsakh / parasang) — a Persian unit of distance, each approx. 5.5–6 km

ai.seo_question: At what minimum travel distance does shortening the prayer (qasr) become obligatory according to Imam al-Baqir in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: Imam Muhammad al-Baqir (AS) declares that the shortening of prayer (qasr) during travel becomes obligatory at the distance of one barid, defined here as four farsakhs (approx. 22–23 km). Al-Tusi records this narration in al-Istibsar to address its apparent conflict with other traditions establishing the threshold at two barids (eight farsakhs); he ultimately reconciles the two by interpreting this report as referring to one leg of a journey for which the traveller intends to return.
